name: Harbourline Tower
blurb: An exterior diagrid that delivered column-free floors on a fifth less steel than a conventional frame.
overview: Harbourline is a 40 storey office tower on a reclaimed waterfront plot. The client wanted open floor plates and a slim silhouette, so we moved the lateral system to the perimeter as a steel diagrid and kept the core to lifts and stairs. Every node was modelled parametrically, and the frame was checked under full wind tunnel loading before a single connection was drawn.

name: Estuary Crossing
blurb: Twin concrete pylons carrying road and light rail across an exposed tidal estuary.
overview: The crossing carries a dual carriageway and a light rail line over a tidal estuary with strong cross winds and an aggressive marine climate. The deck section was refined in the wind tunnel, the pylons were slipformed through two winters, and every stay anchorage was detailed so it can be inspected and replaced without closing the bridge.

name: Ridgeway Process Plant
blurb: A heat recovery rebuild of a continuous process line, installed without a day of lost production.
overview: Ridgeway needed to cut the energy draw of an ageing continuous line without stopping it. We metered the plant for a full season, calibrated a model against what we measured, and phased the heat recovery installation across four planned maintenance windows so the line never went down.

name: Central Station Canopy
blurb: A 92 metre steel and glass canopy raised over platforms that stayed open throughout.
overview: The new canopy shelters six platforms without a single intermediate column. Because the station never closed, the ribs were lifted in night possessions of four hours each, and the temporary stability of the half-built roof was checked at every stage of the sequence.

name: Valley Rail Viaduct
blurb: Precast segments launched span by span across a floodplain, keeping the farmland beneath in use.
overview: The viaduct lifts a new rail alignment clear of a floodplain that the landowners still farm. Piers sit on bored piles founded below the alluvium, and the deck is assembled from precast segments by a launching gantry, so the footprint on the ground below is no wider than the piers themselves.

name: Deepwater Quay
blurb: A piled quay deck for the largest container vessels, built beside berths that never stopped working.
overview: The new quay adds a deep-water berth to a busy terminal. Tubular steel piles were driven from a jack-up platform, the deck was cast in long bays behind a moving cofferdam, and the sequence was planned around the vessel calls at the neighbouring berths so the port lost no traffic.

name: Kingsgate Basement
blurb: A four-level basement dug beside listed buildings, with movement held inside millimetres.
overview: Kingsgate sits hard against two listed facades and a live utility corridor. A secant pile wall propped at three levels holds the ground, and the neighbouring buildings were monitored around the clock, with trigger levels agreed with their owners before the first bucket of spoil came out.

name: Northfield Energy Centre
blurb: A low-carbon expansion tied into live systems inside an eleven day shutdown.
overview: The expansion needed 38 tie-ins to systems that could only be opened during the annual outage. Modules were built and tested off site, every cut was rehearsed in the model first, and the lift plan was sequenced so no two tie-ins ever waited on the same crane.

name: Meadowbank Logistics Hub
blurb: A long-span portal frame delivered from ground investigation to handover in fifteen months.
overview: A distribution shed is a simple structure on an unforgiving programme. Connections were detailed to the fabricator's own shop standards, steel arrived on site in erection order, and the floor slab was poured in bays that followed the frame rather than waiting for it.

name: Albion House Retrofit
blurb: Five new storeys on a 1970s concrete frame, with the tenants staying in throughout.
overview: Nobody had ever calculated the spare capacity in the original frame, so we started with a full survey and load test rather than an assumption. Strengthening was limited to nine columns and one transfer beam, which carries the new lightweight steel storeys without disturbing the occupied floors below.

name: Westbrook Lock Gates
blurb: Replacement lock gates built and load tested on the quay, then set in a single closure.
overview: The gates were too large to assemble inside the chamber, so they were fabricated and load tested on the quayside, then lifted in during one planned closure of the waterway. The drive machinery was commissioned dry before the chamber was flooded again.

name: Parkside Campus
blurb: Teaching buildings in timber and stone, sharing one low temperature heat network.
overview: The campus runs on a ground source heat network that only performs if the buildings are commissioned as one system. Metering was specified at design stage, so performance could be proved against the model before handover rather than argued about afterwards.
